birth.note: Region of Influence: Lahore (Punjab, South Asia)

cultural_layer.festival: Annual Urs at Data Darbar, Lahore
cultural_layer.place: Shrine of Data Ganj Bakhsh, Lahore, Pakistan

poetry.themes: Divine love, mysticism, ethics, spiritual guidance, Sufi metaphysics
poetry.musical_traditions: Qawwali gatherings at his shrine, later expanded by the Chishtiyya order

historical_layer.political_context: Ghaznavid Empire; Lahore emerging as a cultural and spiritual center
historical_layer.spiritual_orders: Early Sufi tradition (pre-Chishti presence in South Asia); deeply connected to the Junaydi Sufi school
historical_layer.influence: Migrated from Ghazni to Lahore on divine inspiration; his influence spread across South Asia through his disciples and writings

movement.summary: Migrated from Ghazni to Lahore on divine inspiration; his influence spread across South Asia through his disciples and writings

teachings: Full name: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Uthman al-Jullabi al-Hujwiri
Known as Data Ganj Bakhsh (“the Bestower of Treasures”), revered as the spiritual patron of Lahore
Author of the famous Persian Sufi treatise Kashf al-Mahjub (Unveiling of the Veiled) — one of the earliest manuals on Sufi thought and practice
Combined scholarship with spirituality: Qur’anic exegesis, Hadith, jurisprudence, and mysticism
Considered a spiritual ancestor of later South Asian Sufi movements (Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiri)
His shrine (Data Darbar) is the largest in South Asia and a major center of Qawwali and Sufi gatherings

historical_layer.political_context: Delhi Sultanate expansion into Sindh; Mongol pressure in Central Asia.
historical_layer.spiritual_orders: Qalandariyya, also linked with Suhrawardiyya and Qadriyya.
